summary: An AJC and UGA poll taken Oct. 7 to 15 found Republican businessman Rick Jackson at 46 percent and Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms at 45 percent for the open governor's seat, a statistical deadlock. The AJC reports Jackson holds a huge self funded money edge and the backing of Gov. Brian Kemp, while Bottoms leans on Democratic enthusiasm and ties Jackson to Trump, health care profits and data centers.

issues.why: Jackson attacks Bottoms' record as Atlanta mayor during the 2020 unrest, while Bottoms says the attacks distort her record.
Bottoms wants full Medicaid expansion and says Jackson profited from a broken health system, while Jackson backs a state waiver with work requirements.
Bottoms calls for a pause on new data centers and questions Jackson's investments, while Jackson notes she approved a Midtown project with incentives.
Jackson says voters care about gas prices, bills and property taxes, while Bottoms pledges to repeal the state grocery tax.
Bottoms used the debate he skipped to press Jackson on how rape exceptions work under Georgia's six week ban, which his campaign says mischaracterizes him.

storylines.title: Bottoms reports 23 million dollar haul
storylines.what: Bottoms raised 23.2 million dollars since August with big DGA help, though Jackson has bought 87 million dollars in general election airtime from mostly his own money.

storylines.title: AJC poll finds a dead heat
storylines.what: Jackson led 46 to 45 among likely voters, with Bottoms ahead among independents and Democrats far more enthusiastic than Republicans.

storylines.title: Jackson keeps distance from Trump
storylines.what: Jackson, who once promised to be Trump's favorite governor, skipped a Trump rally for a Cherokee County event and casts himself as Kemp's heir.

storylines.title: Jackson skips Atlanta Press Club debate
storylines.what: Bottoms debated an empty podium and called Jackson a coward, while Jackson campaigned with Kemp and said voters care about costs, not debates.

storylines.title: Family condemns Jackson crime ad
storylines.what: The family of Secoriea Turner asked Jackson to pull an ad using her mother's 911 call, and his campaign said it will keep highlighting Bottoms' record as mayor.

storylines.title: Lone debate clash over data centers
storylines.what: Bottoms said Jackson cannot be trusted on data centers and tied him to Trump, and Jackson hit her public safety record and her own data center approvals.

storylines.title: Bottoms launches rigged system ad
storylines.what: Bottoms' first on camera attack ad says Jackson made his fortune off a broken health system and touts her grocery tax repeal and Medicaid expansion.

events.title: Skip the televised debate
events.prompt: The Atlanta Press Club debate is set on public TV, and the race is tied. Does the campaign show up, and how does it frame the choice?

opts.label: Debate and hit absence
opts.say: Take the stage and call any no show a coward hiding from voters on a private jet.

opts.label: Debate on the issues
opts.say: Show up and stick to a cost of living message without attacking the opponent's choice.

opts.label: Skip for the trail
opts.say: Skip the debate and campaign with Gov. Kemp, saying voters ask about bills, not debates.

events.title: Data center boom
events.prompt: Data centers are spreading across Georgia and raising worries about power bills and water. What is the policy?

opts.label: Pause new projects
opts.say: Call for a pause on new data center construction until ratepayers are protected.

opts.label: Make them pay their way
opts.say: Allow growth but require data centers to cover their own power and water costs.

opts.label: Keep Georgia open
opts.say: Defend incentives as job creators and attack the opponent's past approvals as hypocrisy.

events.title: Atlanta crime record
events.prompt: Ads are replaying crime from the 2020 unrest in Atlanta, and a victim's family has asked that one be pulled. How does the campaign handle public safety?

opts.label: Condemn the ad
opts.say: Stand with the family, call the ad exploitation and point to police hiring as mayor.

opts.label: Own regrets, look ahead
opts.say: Acknowledge the delayed crackdown was a regret and lay out a public safety plan.

opts.label: Stay on offense
opts.say: Keep the ad up and argue the record shows the opponent abandoned police when needed.

events.title: Medicaid expansion
events.prompt: Georgia has not fully expanded Medicaid and health costs are a central attack in the race. What is the plan?

opts.label: Full expansion
opts.say: Opt into full federal Medicaid expansion and repeal the grocery tax.

opts.label: Waiver with work rules
opts.say: Pursue a state designed expansion waiver with work, education or training requirements.

opts.label: No expansion
opts.say: Reject new Medicaid spending and focus on lowering costs through competition.

regions.name: Atlanta core
regions.note: Deep blue urban counties and Bottoms' home base, where turnout drives Democratic hopes.

regions.name: Inner suburbs
regions.note: Diverse suburbs that flipped Democratic over the last decade and decide statewide races.

regions.name: North Georgia exurbs
regions.note: Fast growing and strongly Republican, the core of Jackson's vote.

regions.name: Middle Georgia and Augusta
regions.note: A mix of Democratic leaning cities and Republican suburbs and military communities.

regions.name: Coast and South Georgia
regions.note: Savannah and Albany lean Democratic while the rural south is solidly Republican.
